models.name: econ_politic_board_guests
models.description: Temporary guest accounts for unauthenticated users identified by device fingerprint with no password requirements. Each guest account is tied to a device identifier and has a short-lived session for browsing without registration. Guests can browse sections and view articles but cannot create content or interact beyond anonymous viewing.

plainFields.name: device_id
plainFields.description: Device fingerprint identifier used to track guest sessions. Must be unique per device for temporary account linkage.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Account creation timestamp indicating when the guest session was initiated.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Last modification timestamp tracking session updates for device fingerprint management.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete timestamp indicating when the guest account was expired or cleared.

models.name: econ_politic_board_members
models.description:
Regular authenticated user accounts with email/password credentials. Stores user profile information including display name and bio text.

Used as the primary identity entity for users within the economic/political discussion board platform. Each account represents a distinct user type that can participate in the platform by creating articles, comments, and managing their profile.

Accounts require email verification before becoming fully active. Passwords are stored as hashes for security, with password reset functionality available for recovery.

The email field is mandatory and must be unique across all members. The display name field is optional, allowing users to choose whether to show a public identifier. The bio field is also optional and provides space for a short profile description.

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description: User's email address used for authentication and communication. Must be unique across all members.

plainFields.name: password_hash
plainFields.description: Password hash used for authentication. Never store plain passwords.

plainFields.name: display_name
plainFields.description: User's display name visible to other users. Maximum 30 characters.

plainFields.name: bio
plainFields.description: User's bio text describing their profile. Maximum 500 characters.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of when this member account was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of when this member account was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of when this member account was deleted. (Null means not deleted.)

models.name: econ_politic_board_member_sessions
models.description:
Member session tracking for authenticated users with JWT access tokens.

Stores session lifecycle information for authenticated members, including authentication context and connection details. Each session belongs to exactly one authenticated member and can have multiple concurrent active sessions.

Session tokens have limited validity (1 hour access, 30 days refresh) to meet security requirements. Session data includes connection metadata (IP address, URL references) for audit purposes.

All sessions follow a strict lifecycle with non-null expiration times to prevent unlimited access tokens. Created and expired timestamps enable session history analysis and security monitoring.

foreignFields.name: member_id
foreignFields.description: Member who owns this session. {@link econ_politic_board_members.id}.

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: IP address of the session connection.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: Connection URL (e.g., /dashboard).

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: Referrer URL from which the user initiated the session.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Session creation timestamp.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Session expiration timestamp (1 hour after creation).

models.name: econ_politic_board_member_password_resets
models.description:
Password reset tokens used for securely resetting member passwords. These tokens are generated upon password reset request and expire after 1 hour to prevent abuse.

Each token is unique and directly associated with a member during the password recovery process. Tokens are marked as used when successfully applied, providing clear audit trail of all password reset activities. The table enforces strict expiration timing to maintain security integrity.

The token must be unique across the system, and tokens should be generated using cryptographically secure random value generation. All token-related operations are managed exclusively through the password reset workflow, not through direct user actions.

foreignFields.name: econ_politic_board_member_id
foreignFields.description: Member who requested password reset. {@link econ_politic_board_members.id}.

plainFields.name: token
plainFields.description: UUID-based token string for password reset verification. Must be unique across all entries for security.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the password reset token was generated.

plainFields.name: expires_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the password reset token expires after 1 hour. Tokens always expire, never "unlimited".

plainFields.name: used_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the token was successfully used to reset the password. Empty if token was never used.

models.name: econ_politic_board_admins
models.description:
Administrator accounts with email/password authentication for managing content and moderating user interactions.

Stores administrative user credentials and basic profile information. Each admin must register with a valid email, and the system handles secure password storage using bcrypt hashing.

Administrators can access all content management features and user moderation tools. Admin accounts persist until explicitly deleted by another administrator.

The system maintains audit trails for account creation and modification using standard timestamps and soft delete support.

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description: Email address used for authentication and system communication. Must be unique across all administrators and valid per email format rules.

plainFields.name: password_hash
plainFields.description: Securely hashed password for authentication, stored using bcrypt. Never store plain text passwords.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of when the admin account was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of when the admin account was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of when the admin account was deleted. If null, the account is active.

models.name: econ_politic_board_admin_sessions
models.description:
Administrator session management with JWT tokens for secure access.

Stores active session records for administrators with access (1-hour) and refresh (30-day) tokens. Each session is tied to a specific administrator and includes connection metadata for audit purposes.

Session tokens expire after 1 hour for access tokens and 30 days for refresh tokens, ensuring secure access management. The session creation timestamp allows for session history analysis and audit trails.

All sessions are recorded with IP address, connection URL, and referrer information to track access patterns and detect security anomalies.

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: IP address of the user connecting from.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: Connection URL used for the session.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: Referrer URL of the client connection.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Session creation timestamp.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Session expiration timestamp (1 hour for access, 30 days for refresh).

models.name: econ_politic_board_admin_password_resets
models.description:
Admin password reset tokens for secure password recovery workflows. Stores temporary reset tokens with 1-hour expiration associated with administrator accounts, facilitating secure password reset processes without storing passwords.

Tokens are generated during password reset requests and expire after 1 hour for security. Each token is tied to a specific administrator record, allowing verification of the request's owner without requiring password storage.

When tokens expire, they're automatically removed from the system, and users must request a new reset link. Soft delete capability ensures token records can be purged after expiration without losing audit history.

plainFields.name: reset_token
plainFields.description: Secure one-time token for password reset requests. Generated as random UUID with SHA-256 hashing for security.

plainFields.name: expires_at
plainFields.description: Token expiration datetime. Set to 1 hour from creation for security.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Token creation timestamp for audit purposes.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete timestamp for record retention policies.

models.name: econ_politic_board_guest_sessions
models.description:
Temporary guest sessions for unauthenticated browsing.

Stores connection context for users who access the platform without logging in. Each session has a short 5-minute expiration period for security. Tracks connection metadata including IP address, URL, and referrer information for audit purposes. Sessions are tied to guest accounts (identified by device fingerprint, not email).

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: IP address used for the session connection.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: Connection URL used to initiate the session.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: Referrer URL that led to this session.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the session was created.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the session expires (5 minutes from creation).

models.name: econ_politic_board_member_email_verifications
models.description:
Verification tokens for new member registration.

Stores tokens sent to members during account creation to verify their email addresses. Each token is valid for exactly 1 hour and is tied to a specific member account for verification tracking.

Tokens expire automatically and are not manually managed through the application. These tokens are created during the registration process and serve as the mechanism for confirming a member's email address.

Unlike password resets, these tokens cannot be regenerated without creating a new account, ensuring email verification is a one-time process during initial sign-up.

foreignFields.name: member_id
foreignFields.description: Member this verification token belongs to. {@link econ_politic_board_members.id}

plainFields.name: email_verification_token
plainFields.description: Unique token string sent to member's email for verification. Used to confirm email address during registration.

plainFields.name: expires_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp indicating when this token expires (1 hour from creation).

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp indicating when this token was created (sent to member's email).

models.name: econ_politic_board_system_configs
models.description:
System-wide configuration settings and feature flags that control platform behavior, accessibility, and user experience across the entire application.

Stores key-value pairs for configuration parameters, where the key represents the setting name (e.g., 'comment_min_length', 'article_max_tags') and the value represents the current setting value. This table also includes human-readable descriptions for each configuration setting.

These configuration settings can be modified through the platform's administrative interface to adjust platform behavior without requiring code changes. System configurations include settings related to content rules, user experience features, and platform capabilities.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: Unique configuration key name (e.g., 'comment_min_length', 'article_max_tags'). Used to identify this configuration setting.

plainFields.name: value
plainFields.description: Current value of the configuration setting (e.g., '10', '5'). Can be a number, string, or boolean represented as string.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Human-readable description of what this configuration setting does and its purpose in the system.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this configuration setting was added to the system.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this configuration setting was last modified.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this configuration setting was deleted (soft delete).

models.name: econ_politic_board_articles
models.description:
Core articles representing economic or political discussions written by users.

Articles serve as the primary user-generated content for the platform, allowing members to share their perspectives on various topics. Each article is associated with a specific section (Politics, Economy, Current Affairs) and has a clear author relationship.

The title field captures the main topic of the article with a minimum of 5 characters for sufficient context and maximum of 100 characters to prevent overly verbose titles.
The content field requires at least 50 characters to ensure substantive discussion content is provided rather than empty or minimal entries.
The article structure follows an append-only pattern for historical tracking with no direct modifications to past content, instead creating new article versions for edits.

foreignFields.name: section_id
foreignFields.description: Section the article belongs to. {@link econ_politic_board_sections.id}

plainFields.name: title
plainFields.description: Main topic or headline of the article. Must be 5-100 characters for contextual relevance while remaining concise.

plainFields.name: content
plainFields.description: Core discussion content of the article. Minimum 50 characters ensures substantial contribution rather than minimal content.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: When the article was first created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: When the article was last modified.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: When the article was marked for deletion (soft delete) with no immediate physical removal from storage.

models.name: econ_politic_board_article_attachments
models.description:
File attachments for articles, supporting document and image uploads with metadata.

Stores all files attached to articles including images, PDFs, and other document formats. Each attachment is linked to a specific article, with metadata about the file name, size, type, and storage location. The attachment is only linked to a single article and cannot be shared across multiple articles.

File types are limited to standard web formats (images: JPEG, PNG, GIF; documents: PDF, DOCX, XLSX) to ensure security and compatibility. Each article can have up to 10 attachments with a maximum total size of 50MB as specified in the business requirements.

Attachments are stored with a timestamp for creation, update, and soft deletion for audit purposes while the original article content remains accessible.

foreignFields.name: econ_politic_board_article_id
foreignFields.description: Article attachment belongs to article's {@link econ_politic_board_articles.id}.

plainFields.name: file_name
plainFields.description: Original file name of the attachment, including extension.

plainFields.name: file_type
plainFields.description: MIME type of the file (e.g., image/jpeg, application/pdf).

plainFields.name: file_size
plainFields.description: File size in bytes, limited to a total of 50MB per article across all attachments.

plainFields.name: storage_location
plainFields.description: Where the file is stored (URL or path), typically a cloud storage path.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the attachment was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the attachment was last modified.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the attachment was soft-deleted, allowing audit while maintaining article integrity.

models.name: econ_politic_board_article_tags
models.description:
Tag values used for categorization and filtering of articles.

Each article can have up to five tags, with a maximum length of 20 characters and no spaces. Tags provide an additional layer of content organization beyond the article's section.

Tag management is done through the article creation and editing workflows, not as standalone entities. The tag values are stored as strings with strict validation to ensure consistency across the platform.

foreignFields.name: econ_politic_board_articles_id
foreignFields.description: Article to which this tag is associated. {@link econ_politic_board_articles.id}

plainFields.name: tag
plainFields.description: Tag value used for categorization of an article. Maximum length: 20 characters. Tags must not contain spaces.

models.name: econ_politic_board_article_versions
models.description:
Stores historical versions of article content changes with full content snapshots for auditing and version rollback capabilities.

Each version records the exact content state at the time of article editing, maintaining a complete history of changes without loss of data. Version history is automatically generated on every article edit, requiring no user intervention for version tracking.

The table supports full content retrieval for any version, enabling features like 'View Previous Version' while preserving the ability to compare changes over time. Historical versions remain intact even if the original article is edited, deleted, or modified, ensuring a complete audit trail of all content modifications.

foreignFields.name: article_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the parent article. {@link econ_politic_board_articles.id}.

plainFields.name: content
plainFields.description: Full article content at the time of version creation, including all text and formatted structure. Stores the complete content that was active during the article edit.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this version was created (matches the point of article edit).

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this version was last modified (for historical consistency, same as created_at but maintained for completeness).

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this version was soft-deleted (if applicable for audit purposes), null indicates active version.

models.name: econ_politic_board_admin_requests
models.description:
Tracks administrator role requests from users, allowing regular users to request administrator privileges with reasons and status tracking for super administrators to review.

Each request includes the user's reason for requesting admin access (minimum 50 characters), the current status of the request (pending/approved/rejected), and timestamps for creation and updates. Super administrators review these requests to manage administrative roles across the platform.

This table maintains a clear record of all admin access requests to ensure transparency and accountability in the role management process.

foreignFields.name: user_id
foreignFields.description: User who made the request. {@link econ_politic_board_members.id}.

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: Reason provided by the user for requesting administrator privileges. Must be at least 50 characters in length and meet specific content guidelines to ensure proper context for review.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current status of the administrator request. Valid values: 'pending', 'approved', 'rejected'. This field determines the action to be taken by super administrators for each request.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the administrator request was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the administrator request was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the request was soft-deleted. Used for audit trails while removing it from active views.

models.name: econ_politic_board_profiles
models.description:
User profile storage for display names and bios with business constraints.

Stores additional user information beyond the core identity provided in the authentication system. Profile data is optional for users to provide and can be updated at any time, but cannot be set to null permanently (must maintain minimal user visibility information). The display name field enforces a maximum length of 30 characters as specified in the business rules.

The bio field provides a text-based description for user profiles with a maximum length of 500 characters for consistent content presentation across the platform. Both profile fields are optional but should be present for users who choose to establish a profile.

foreignFields.name: econ_politic_board_members_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the core member identity

plainFields.name: display_name
plainFields.description: Custom user display name visible to others. Maximum 30 characters as per business rules.

plainFields.name: bio
plainFields.description: User profile bio text for additional self-description. Maximum 500 characters as per business rules.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Date and time the profile was created, used for historical tracking.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Date and time the profile was last updated, used for tracking changes.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Date and time the profile was marked as deleted (soft delete).

models.name: econ_politic_board_sections
models.description:
Section entities representing topics like Politics, Economy, Current Affairs with unique names and descriptions.

Sections serve as organizational containers for articles, allowing users and administrators to categorize content into distinct topic areas. Each section is characterized by a unique name and descriptive summary, providing context for content within that category.

Administrators manage sections through creation, editing, and viewing operations. Sections are referenced by articles to establish their categorization, forming one-to-many relationships where each article belongs to exactly one section.

Section names must be unique across the entire platform and follow the system's uniqueness requirements. All sections support soft deletion for content management without permanent data loss.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: Section name (e.g., Politics, Economy) with maximum 50 characters, must be unique.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Section description up to 250 characters detailing the section's purpose and content scope.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the section was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the section was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete timestamp; section is considered deleted when this field has a value.
